results.title: First-exec warm-up (harness fix verification)
results.desc: Throwaway first exec absorbs the suspected session warm-up
results.prose: The empty-exec pattern from four cycles (whichever exec test runs first in the battery returns empty; retries always clean) pointed to a first-exec session warm-up on the gateway path. This cycle I added the candidate fix: a throwaway warm-up exec before the battery proper. It returned 'warmup-ok' — the warm-up exec itself succeeded, so the battery's first REAL exec will reveal whether the pattern is truly positional. If TV-ENV/TV-FS all pass this cycle, the warm-up absorbs whatever the transient is.
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait ready; one exec 'echo warmup-ok'; DeleteSandbox; then run the regression battery normally.

results.title: Sandbox count tracks pod lifecycle (spec OSG-SBX-01)
results.desc: Listing reflects create (running) and delete promptly — the count input
results.prose: Random spec draw: openshell-gateway-sandbox-count.spec.md (OSG-SBX-01 — event-driven active_sandbox_count maintained from a pod watch, incrementing on Running/Pending and decrementing on exit, with periodic self-heal). The control-plane watch isn't visible from a sandbox SA, but the user-facing surface it feeds is: our gateway's listing showed the new sandbox while running and dropped it within seconds of delete. The operator's delete-confirmation number is built on data that tracks reality this promptly — and this cycle's create/list/delete churn exercises exactly the Pending→Running transition the spec says must NOT double-count.
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait ready; ListSandboxes contains name; DeleteSandbox; wait 5s; ListSandboxes no longer contains name.
